snippet.title: 6 Famous Stars Who Sadly Passed Away After 90
snippet.description:
6 famous stars who sadly passed away after 90. From Oscar winners Gene Hackman, Robert Duvall and Eva Marie Saint to Lassie’s June Lockhart, Top Gun’s Tom Skerritt and Star Trek’s Walter Koenig, these legends lived long, remarkable lives and gave us decades of unforgettable movies and TV. Here’s a look back at the roles that made them stars.

In this tribute, we remember:
⭐ Eva Marie Saint (102) – Oscar winner for On the Waterfront, North by Northwest, Superman Returns
⭐ June Lockhart (100) – The mom on Lassie and Lost in Space, Meet Me in St. Louis
⭐ Robert Duvall (95) – The Godfather, Apocalypse Now, Lonesome Dove
⭐ Gene Hackman (95) – Two-time Oscar winner for The French Connection and Unforgiven
⭐ Tom Skerritt (93) – Viper in Top Gun, Steel Magnolias, Emmy winner for Picket Fences
⭐ Walter Koenig (90) – Ensign Chekov on the original Star Trek

These Hollywood legends were part of our lives for generations, from golden-age classics and family TV favorites to the blockbusters we still watch today. They reminded us that a long life can be a full one, and they will be truly missed.

snippet.title: 4 Top Gun Stars Who Sadly Died Recently
snippet.description:
4 Top Gun stars who sadly passed away. From Val Kilmer’s unforgettable Iceman to Tom Skerritt’s Viper, James Tolkan’s Stinger and Clarence Gilyard’s Sundown, the cast of the 1986 classic has lost some of its most beloved faces. Here’s a look back at the roles and moments that made Top Gun legendary.

In this tribute, we remember:
⭐ Val Kilmer – Iceman in Top Gun and Top Gun: Maverick, Tombstone, Batman Forever
⭐ Tom Skerritt – Viper in Top Gun, Steel Magnolias, Emmy winner for Picket Fences
⭐ James Tolkan – Stinger in Top Gun, Principal Strickland in Back to the Future
⭐ Clarence Gilyard – Sundown in Top Gun, Theo in Die Hard, Walker, Texas Ranger

These stars helped make Top Gun one of the biggest movies of the 1980s and a film fans still quote today, from “I feel the need for speed” to “Your ego is writing checks your body can’t cash.” They will be truly missed.

snippet.title: 5 Country Legends We Lost Recently
snippet.description:
5 country legends we lost recently. From Hall of Famer John Anderson to outlaw rebel David Allan Coe, Grand Ole Opry icon Jeannie Seely, and the songwriter behind “The Gambler,” Don Schlitz, country music said goodbye to some of its greatest voices. Here’s a look back at the songs and moments that made them unforgettable.

In this tribute, we remember:
⭐ John Anderson – Country Music Hall of Famer, Swingin’, Straight Tequila Night, Seminole Wind
⭐ Johnny Rodriguez – Country’s first major Mexican-American star, six #1 hits, Ridin’ My Thumb to Mexico
⭐ Jeannie Seely – Grammy winner for Don’t Touch Me, most Grand Ole Opry appearances in history
⭐ David Allan Coe – Outlaw country legend, wrote Take This Job and Shove It, You Never Even Called Me by My Name
⭐ Don Schlitz – Songwriter of The Gambler for Kenny Rogers and Forever and Ever, Amen for Randy Travis

These country music legends were the soundtrack of our lives, from honky-tonk jukeboxes and Saturday nights at the Opry to the classic country radio we grew up with. Their songs will live on forever.

snippet.title: 10 Beloved Actresses Who Passed Away in the Last Few Days
snippet.description:
These beloved actresses made us laugh, moved us to tears, and kept us glued to the screen for decades. In this tribute, we remember 10 unforgettable actresses who passed away recently, and the iconic roles that made us love them.

Canadian-American actress, Catherine O’Hara, died of a pulmonary embolism, on January 30, at the age of 71. She was best known for her roles, as Kate McCallister, in the Home Alone films. Delia Deetz, in the 1988 film, Beetlejuice. Cookie Fleck, in the 2000 film, Best in Show. And Moira Rose, in the television sitcom, Schitt’s Creek, for which she won an Emmy Award.

American actress, Valerie Perrine, died of complications from Parkinson’s disease, on March 23, at the age of 82. She was best known for her roles, as Honey Bruce, in the 1974 film, Lenny, for which she received an Oscar nomination. And Eve Teschmacher, in the 1978 film, Superman.

American actress, Eva Marie Saint, died of natural causes, on October 6, at the age of 102. She was best known for her roles, as Edie Doyle, in the 1954 film, On the Waterfront, for which she won an Academy Award. Eve Kendall, in the 1959 Alfred Hitchcock film, North by Northwest. And Martha Kent, in the 2006 film, Superman Returns.

American actress, Anne Schedeen, died peacefully, in June, at the age of 77. She was best known for her role, as Kate Tanner, in the television sitcom, ALF.

Irish actress, Brenda Fricker, died on July 16, at the age of 81. She was best known for her roles, as Bridget Brown, in the 1989 film, My Left Foot, for which she won an Academy Award. The Pigeon Lady, in the 1992 film, Home Alone 2: Lost in New York. And Megan Roach, in the BBC drama series, Casualty.

American singer, songwriter, and actress, Dolly Parton, died of cancer, on August 25, at the age of 80. She was best known for her songs, Jolene, I Will Always Love You, and 9 to 5, and for her roles, as Doralee Rhodes, in the 1980 film, 9 to 5. And Truvy Jones, in the 1989 film, Steel Magnolias.

American actress, Judy Pace, died in her sleep, on March 11, at the age of 83. She was best known for her roles, as Vickie Fletcher, in the television series, Peyton Place. Linda Sayers, in the 1971 television film, Brian’s Song. And Pat Walters, in the television series, The Young Lawyers, for which she won an NAACP Image Award.

American actress, and singer, Ann Blyth, died of natural causes, on June 24, at the age of 98. She was best known for her roles, as Veda Pierce, in the 1945 film, Mildred Pierce, for which she received an Oscar nomination. And her performances in the MGM musicals The Great Caruso, Rose Marie, and Kismet.

English actress, Jane Lapotaire, died on March 5, at the age of 81. She was best known for her roles, as Marie Curie, in the 1977 television miniseries, Marie Curie. Édith Piaf, in the stage play, Piaf, for which she won a Tony Award and an Olivier Award. And Princess Alice, in the Netflix series, The Crown.

American actress, Hayden Panettiere, died on August 16, at the age of 36. She was best known for her roles, as Claire Bennet, in the television series, Heroes. Juliette Barnes, in the television series, Nashville. Kirby Reed, in the Scream films. And the voice of Princess Dot, in the 1998 film, A Bug’s Life.

Which actress will you miss the most? Share your favorite memory in the comments.

Thank you for watching. If you liked this video, hit the subscribe button to receive more like it in the future.

snippet.title: 3 marriages Hollywood couldn’t break
snippet.description:
Here are 3 marriages Hollywood couldn’t break.

Michael J. Fox married Tracy Pollan in 1988. Three years later, at just 29, he was diagnosed with Parkinson's. For over 35 years since, she's never once left his side. He's said she would've been forgiven if she had. She didn't. 'In sickness and in health,' he remembers her whispering the day he told her. 'That she was going to hang on and get me through it.

George Clooney swore for years he'd never get married. Then he met Amal Alamuddin, a human rights lawyer, at a dinner party in 2013. Every promise he'd made to himself disappeared. They married in 2014. He's said she completely rewrote what he thought his life would look like. In 2017, they welcomed twins, Ella and Alexander.

John Legend met Chrissy Teigen on a music video set in 2006. He proposed in the Maldives five years later, then serenaded her with the song he wrote about her — 'All of Me.' In 2020, after they lost a pregnancy, he stood on stage and dedicated a song to her live, saying their love would 'never break.' This year, they celebrated 13 years of marriage. She said she'd choose him again, over and over.

snippet.title: He Needs 24 Hour Care but Still Dreams of Making Music
snippet.description:
Phil Collins spent decades commanding stadiums with his voice and drums, but today his life looks very different. After years of nerve damage, knee problems, surgeries, and declining mobility, even simple movements can be difficult.

What makes his story so powerful is that despite everything his body has been through, Phil still hasn’t completely let go of music. He still talks about creating again if his health allows it.

snippet.title: He Gives Her $3 Million for Every Year They Stay Married
snippet.description:
Michael Douglas and Catherine Zeta-Jones have one of Hollywood’s most talked-about marriages — and their reported prenup has surprised people for years. Michael was already a major Hollywood star worth hundreds of millions when they married, and reports claimed the agreement could be worth millions for every year of marriage, with even more at stake if he was ever unfaithful.

More than 25 years later, they’re still together. So what do you think — smart protection, or an unbelievable deal?

snippet.title: He Makes $50 Million Per Movie but Lives Like He’s Broke
snippet.description:
Harrison Ford has spent more than 50 years becoming one of the most recognizable stars in Hollywood, but off camera, he has always seemed much more comfortable living a quiet and simple life. Even after starring in legendary movies like Star Wars and Indiana Jones and earning millions along the way, Harrison never appeared interested in showing off his wealth.

Instead, he has often focused on helping people who need it most and supporting causes that can make a real difference in someone’s life. That’s one of the reasons so many fans see Harrison Ford as more than just a movie star.
